title: The Ellis and Baldwin test of the Cosmic Dipole: Exploring the impact of multiple flux density cuts
comment: 26 pages, 14 figures, accepted for publication in Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics (JCAP)
summary: The cosmic dipole tension - the discrepancy between the Cosmic Microwave Background kinematic dipole and the matter dipole inferred from all-sky surveys poses a significant challenge to the Cosmological Principle, which dictates that the universe is homogeneous and isotropic at the largest scales. Traditional measurement of the matter dipole requires selecting an appropriate limiting flux and calculating the dipolar modulation using sources brighter than the flux. This approach, however, ignores the shape of the source luminosity function (LF) and deprives the analysis of this crucial information. In this study, we present a new approach to calculate the matter dipole by integrating the source flux distribution into the analysis. We achieve this by dividing the catalogue into disjoint flux bins and simultaneously fitting the matter dipole across them. For non-power-law LFs, this method gives a higher Bayes factor - and hence a better description of the matter dipole - as compared to the traditional approach. The method works best when the flux cuts are selected in regions where the LF's shape changes significantly. We discuss the feasibility of this method for upcoming cosmological surveys and show that it has the potential to yield decisive results at both radio and infrared wavelengths.

AI.tldr: They propose a new method to measure the matter dipole by using flux-binned source data, improving upon traditional techniques that ignore luminosity function shape, leading to better fits and promising results for future surveys.
AI.motivation: Address the cosmic dipole tension which challenges the Cosmological Principle by improving the measurement of the matter dipole in the universe.
AI.method: Calculate the matter dipole by integrating the source flux distribution into the analysis, dividing the catalogue into disjoint flux bins, and simultaneously fitting the matter dipole across these bins, rather than relying on a limiting flux threshold.
AI.result: The new method yields a higher Bayes factor for non-power-law luminosity functions, providing a better description of the matter dipole. It is most effective when flux cuts are chosen where the luminosity function shape changes significantly and is feasible for upcoming cosmological surveys at radio and infrared wavelengths.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating the flux distribution of sources into the dipole analysis offers a more robust measurement of the matter dipole, potentially resolving some aspects of the cosmic dipole tension and improving constraints on cosmological isotropy and homogeneity.

title: GINKAKU: Scalable Cosmological Structure Formation Simulation Code and Post-processing Pipeline
summary: We introduce GINKAKU, a new cosmological $N$-body code developed for the Dark Quest II (DQ2) simulation campaign and designed for controlled ensemble production across the cosmological model space required by next-generation galaxy surveys, including massive neutrinos and clustering dark energy. Built on the FDPS framework, GINKAKU couples a TreePM gravity solver with a linear-response treatment of external source terms for components not evolved as $N$-body particles, formulated in the $N$-body gauge. This design incorporates massive-neutrino perturbations, general-relativistic corrections, early-time radiation perturbations, and dark-energy clustering with non-unit effective sound speed at the linear level, while preserving Newtonian particle dynamics on subhorizon scales. The code is validated through internal convergence studies and cross-comparisons with GADGET, PKDGRAV3, and RAMSES on shared initial conditions: code-to-code differences in the nonlinear power spectrum can be reduced below $\sim1\%$ level by tuning internal accuracy parameters, and we identify a production-grade fiducial setting achieving this control at modest cost. We apply GINKAKU to an initial set of DQ2 production runs -- eight cosmological models with $3,000^3$ particles in boxes up to $4\,h^{-1}\mathrm{Gpc}$ -- processed by a renewed post-processing pipeline that reduces the inter-resolution spread of the halo mass function to $\sim 1\%$ and includes halo-shape measurements for intrinsic-alignment statistics. The scale-dependent-growth cosmologies reproduce the expected nonlinear signatures of massive neutrinos and clustering dark energy, demonstrating suitability for emulator-scale production. A total matter power spectrum emulator from these runs is presented in an accompanying paper. (abridged)

AI.tldr: GINKAKU is a new cosmological $N$-body code integrating massive neutrinos and clustering dark energy effects with high accuracy and efficiency, validated against major codes, and applied to large-scale simulations for next-generation galaxy surveys.
AI.motivation: To develop a robust and accurate cosmological $N$-body simulation tool suitable for next-generation galaxy surveys, incorporating massive neutrinos and clustering dark energy effects with controlled ensemble production across cosmological models.
AI.method: Development of GINKAKU code based on the FDPS framework, coupling a TreePM gravity solver with linear-response treatment for external source terms in the $N$-body gauge, including massive neutrino perturbations, relativistic corrections, radiation perturbations, and dark-energy clustering, validated through convergence studies and code comparisons with GADGET, PKDGRAV3, and RAMSES.
AI.result: Achieved code-to-code agreement in nonlinear power spectrum below ~1%, identified efficient fiducial accuracy settings, produced large-scale cosmological simulations with controlled halo mass function variance (~1%), and successfully reproduced nonlinear signatures of massive neutrinos and clustering dark energy, confirming suitability for emulator-scale use.
AI.conclusion: GINKAKU provides a highly accurate, efficient, and versatile cosmological $N$-body code that integrates key physical effects beyond standard Newtonian dynamics, enabling precision cosmological modeling required for upcoming galaxy surveys and large ensemble productions.

title: Dark Quest II: A Wide-Coverage Neural Network Emulator of the Nonlinear Matter Power Spectrum Across Extended Cosmologies
comment: 53 pages, 44 figures, emulator code available at https://github.com/DarkQuestCosmology/dark_emulator2_public
summary: \textsc{DarkEmulator2} is a neural network emulator of the nonlinear matter power spectrum in a nine-dimensional $w_0 w_a νo \mathrm{CDM}$ parameter space, developed as the emulator component of the \textsc{Dark Quest II} (DQ2) program. It is trained on simulations generated with the \textsc{Ginkaku} code, whose numerical implementation, accuracy tests, and post-processing pipeline are described in the companion paper. The design follows a unified strategy: in addition to the cosmological parameter vector, we supplement the neural network's inputs with three families of physically motivated auxiliary quantities -- the linear matter power spectrum, descriptors of the simulation resolution, and a low-dimensional summary of the initial Gaussian random field -- that are expected to improve generalization across the parameter space. Training a single network jointly across three simulation resolution tiers allows the emulator to exploit a small number of high-resolution simulations while retaining broad coverage from lower-resolution simulations. For a $L_{\mathrm{box}}=1\,\hiGpc$ box with $N=3000^{3}$ particles, the emulator reproduces the simulated matter power spectrum to subpercent accuracy up to the particle Nyquist scale, $k_{\mathrm{Ny}}\simeq 10\,\hMpci$. The emulator remains accurate over the calibrated wavenumber range, while its highest-$k$ predictions depend on the simulation resolution and shot noise. We validate the emulator on independent test suites and, through a cross-comparison with several public emulators and widely used fitting formulas, characterize the inter-model consistency and the parameter-dependent trends in their residuals.

AI.tldr: DarkEmulator2 is a neural network emulator for the nonlinear matter power spectrum in a 9D cosmological space, trained on multi-resolution simulations using augmented inputs to enhance accuracy and generalization, achieving subpercent accuracy validated against independent data and public emulators.
AI.motivation: To create an accurate and generalizable emulator for the nonlinear matter power spectrum over a high-dimensional cosmological parameter space, improving upon prior models.
AI.method: Develop a neural network-based emulator trained on high-resolution and lower-resolution simulations generated with the Ginkaku code; augment inputs with physically motivated auxiliary quantities (linear matter power spectrum, simulation resolution descriptors, and Gaussian random field summaries) to improve generalization; train a single network across multiple resolution tiers.
AI.result: The emulator achieves subpercent accuracy in reproducing the nonlinear matter power spectrum up to the Nyquist scale for high-resolution simulations; maintains accuracy across calibrated wavenumber range; validation against independent tests and public emulators shows strong consistency and well-characterized residual trends.
AI.conclusion: A unified approach combining neural networks with physically motivated auxiliary inputs and multi-resolution training effectively emulates the nonlinear matter power spectrum with high accuracy over a complex cosmological parameter space, offering improved generalization and reliability compared to existing models.

title: Exploring non-Poisson satellite occupation in HOD models and its impact on 2- and 3-point galaxy clustering
summary: Understanding the connection between galaxies and dark matter halos is a central challenge in modern cosmology. The Halo Occupation Distribution (HOD) framework provides a widely used statistical description of how galaxies populate dark matter halos, enabling precise modelling of galaxy clustering. A common assumption in standard HOD models is that the number of satellite galaxies follows a Poisson distribution at fixed halo mass. In this work, we revisit this assumption and introduce the Conway-Maxwell-Poisson (CMP) distribution as a minimal extension of of the Poisson model, which add a single parameter, $ν$, to explore sub- and super-Poisson behaviour. We derive analytical approximations for the CMP expectation parameter $λ$ and develop a numerical scheme that smoothly connects small- and large-$λ$ regimes, achieving $\sim5\%$ accuracy for $0.5 < ν< 2$. Using the \texttt{HODDIES} package, we study the impact of non-Poisson satellite occupations on mock galaxy catalogues and clustering statistics. Variations in the variance of the satellite occupation significantly affect small-scale clustering, producing deviations of up to $10\%$ in projected clustering and $5\%$ in the monopole and quadrupole. We further investigate higher-order statistics using counts-in-cylinders (CiC) and the tree-level galaxy bispectrum. CiC statistics are highly sensitive to changes in the variance, with variations up to $\sim30\%$, while the tree-level galaxy bispectrum (in the Sugiyama basis) is only weakly affected ($<2\%$ up to $k_\mathrm{max} = 0.3$). These results suggest that non-Poisson satellite statistics are important for small-scale analyses, but should have a limited impact on cosmological constraints from power spectrum and bispectrum measurements using large scales $k_\mathrm{max} < 0.3$.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the CMP distribution to model satellite galaxy counts beyond the Poisson assumption, showing significant effects on small-scale clustering statistics but minimal impact on large-scale cosmological measurements.
AI.motivation: The standard assumption that satellite galaxy numbers follow a Poisson distribution at fixed halo mass may be oversimplified and needs to be revisited to better model galaxy clustering.
AI.method: Introduce the Conway-Maxwell-Poisson (CMP) distribution as an extension of the Poisson model by adding a parameter ν to capture sub- and super-Poisson satellite occupation behavior; derive analytical approximations and develop a numerical scheme for the CMP parameter λ; utilize the HODDIES package to simulate galaxy catalogues and analyze clustering and higher-order statistics.
AI.result: The CMP model accurately captures satellite occupation variance with ~5% accuracy for certain ν ranges; non-Poisson satellite occupations cause significant deviations in small-scale clustering (up to 10% in projected clustering and 5% in monopole and quadrupole); counts-in-cylinders statistics are very sensitive (up to 30% variations), while the galaxy bispectrum is only weakly affected (<2% up to k_max=0.3).
AI.conclusion: Non-Poisson satellite galaxy occupation statistics substantially influence small-scale clustering analyses but have limited impact on cosmological constraints derived from large-scale power spectrum and bispectrum measurements (k_max < 0.3).

title: Multi-mission Observations of GS 1354-64 during the 2025-26 Outburst: First Results
comment: 12 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables (accepted for publication in ApJ)
summary: The Galactic transient black hole GS 1354-64 recently showed a new outburst, which has been continuously monitored by {\it MAXI}, {\it NuSTAR} and {\it Insight-HXMT} missions. The ongoing $2025-26$ outburst shows a slow-rise with an unusual short period ($\sim 3$~days) of X-ray flare of peak flux $\sim 1.4$~Crab, followed by another relatively weak flare of intensity $\sim 0.8$ Crab. The source is observed to evolve through `canonical' spectral states in a Hardness-Intensity Diagram (HID) during rising phase of the outburst, however subsequent outburst profile did not follow the reverse trend of the HID. A rapid evolution of Quasi-periodic Oscillation (QPO) frequencies ($\sim 0.07-4$ Hz) is observed during hard/intermediate spectral states without any signature of QPOs in the soft state. The evolution of the observed low frequency QPOs shows a monotonically increasing (rising phase) as well as decreasing (decay phase) signature, which are further studied with the propagating oscillatory shock model to understand the nature of the evolution of the shock wave, responsible for the origin of the observed QPOs. The broadband energy spectra from {\it NuSTAR} ($3-70$ keV) and {\it Insight-HXMT} ($2-60$ keV) are well described by thermal (\textit{diskbb}) and reflection (\textit{relxill}) model components, indicating a strong signature of a relativistic reflection feature. Using `canonical' softer state observations, we found the source to be maximally rotating with $a_k \sim 0.998$ and inclination angle to be as $i \sim 63^\circ - 70^\circ$, which are consistent with earlier reports.

AI.tldr: GS 1354-64's 2025-26 outburst shows unique X-ray flare behavior, canonical spectral state transitions, and evolving QPOs explained by a shock model. Spectral analysis indicates near-maximal black hole spin and consistent inclination.
AI.motivation: To study the new outburst of the Galactic transient black hole GS 1354-64, focusing on its spectral and timing properties to understand the accretion dynamics and QPO origins during the 2025-26 event.
AI.method: Continuous monitoring of GS 1354-64 by MAXI, NuSTAR, and Insight-HXMT during the 2025-26 outburst. Analysis of spectral states through Hardness-Intensity Diagrams, timing studies of Quasi-periodic Oscillations (QPOs), and broadband spectral fitting using diskbb and relxill models. QPO evolution was interpreted with the propagating oscillatory shock model.
AI.result: The source displayed a slow-rise outburst with atypical short X-ray flares. It transitioned through canonical spectral states in the rising phase but did not follow the reverse trend in the decay phase. QPO frequencies evolved rapidly (~0.07-4 Hz) only in hard/intermediate states, exhibiting a monotonic increase and decrease in rising and decay phases respectively. Broadband spectra revealed strong relativistic reflection. The black hole showed near-maximal spin (a_k ~ 0.998) and an inclination angle between 63°-70°, consistent with prior findings.
AI.conclusion: The study confirms the presence of relativistic reflection and strong spin in GS 1354-64 during the 2025-26 outburst, with QPO evolution well explained by a propagating oscillatory shock model, providing insights into the accretion shock dynamics and the black hole spin and inclination consistent with past measurements.

title: Measuring the Hubble constant with strongly lensed gravitational waves from space-based detector networks
summary: The measurement of the Hubble constant $H_0$ plays a central role in modern cosmology. In this work, we investigate the potential of strongly lensed gravitational-wave (SLGW) signals from massive binary black hole mergers to constrain $H_0$ using future space-based detector networks. We consider two observational scenarios: one in which the source redshift is unknown, and another in which it is independently determined through electromagnetic observations. We show that meaningful constraints on $H_0$ can still be achieved without source-redshift information, provided that the lens redshift is known. For individual SLGW events, the joint Taiji+LISA analysis improves the measurement precision of $H_0$ by approximately a factor of two compared with the Taiji-only configuration. Extending the analysis to the population level, we combine five simulated SLGW events and find that the uncertainty in $H_0$, quantified by the 95\% credible interval, reaches the $1.1\times10^{-1}$ level when the source redshift is treated as unknown, and further improves to $4.2\times10^{-2}$ when the source redshift is independently measured. Our results demonstrate that joint space-based gravitational-wave observations can substantially enhance the cosmological capability of SLGW events and provide a promising avenue for precision measurements of the Hubble constant.

AI.tldr: This study shows that future space-based gravitational-wave detectors using strongly lensed signals from massive black hole mergers can tightly constrain the Hubble constant, improving precision substantially, especially with joint observations and known source redshifts.
AI.motivation: To address the challenge of precisely measuring the Hubble constant $H_0$, which is critical for modern cosmology, by exploring new methods using gravitational-wave observations.
AI.method: Analyzing strongly lensed gravitational-wave signals from massive binary black hole mergers detected by future space-based detector networks (Taiji and LISA), considering scenarios with and without known source redshifts, incorporating joint detector analyses and simulated event populations.
AI.result: Joint analysis of Taiji and LISA improves $H_0$ measurement precision by a factor of two over Taiji alone. Population-level constraints using five simulated events reduce the 95% credible interval uncertainty on $H_0$ to 0.11 without source redshift and to 0.042 with source redshift known.
AI.conclusion: Strongly lensed gravitational-wave events observed by combined space-based detectors provide a powerful method for precise $H_0$ measurement, even without source redshift information if lens redshift is known, significantly advancing cosmological parameter estimation capabilities.

title: The strength of Type-C quasi-periodic oscillations in black hole X-ray binaries correlates with the jet inclination
comment: Accepted for publication on MNRAS; 9 pages, 6 Figures
summary: X-ray quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) are a characteristic feature of low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs). These oscillations have been studied for decades and revealed a rich and complex phenomenology that is still not fully understood. RXTE archival studies have shown that the amplitude of these oscillations differs significantly between black holes (BH) with high or low inclination. Yet, the actual dependence on inclination has never been adequately estimated. Thanks to the improvement of inclination measurements through radio observations and the recent observations by the HXMT satellite, we quantified for the first time the dependence of Type-C QPO amplitudes on the jet inclination of individual BH LMXBs. Our analysis reveals the presence of a significant linear correlation up to 8 Hz, strengthening the case for a ''geometrical'' origin of the QPOs. In addition, for a given QPO frequency, we observe systematically lower amplitudes during the decay of outbursts compared to the rise. This data collection represents a key benchmark for any QPO model. Our comparison with the predictions from a precessing hot flow shows that the amplitude of the QPOs can be reproduced by this scenario if the spin-orbit misalignment is at least $\approx$10-15$^\circ$.

AI.tldr: This paper quantifies for the first time how Type-C QPO amplitudes in black hole low-mass X-ray binaries depend linearly on jet inclination, supporting a geometrical origin of QPOs and confirming model predictions with spin-orbit misalignment of about 10-15 degrees.
AI.motivation: The study aims to clarify the dependence of Type-C QPO amplitudes on the inclination of black hole low-mass X-ray binaries, which had not been adequately estimated despite decades of research.
AI.method: Utilizing improved inclination measurements from radio observations and recent HXMT satellite data, the authors analyzed the correlation of QPO amplitude with jet inclination across individual black hole LMXBs.
AI.result: They established a significant linear correlation between QPO amplitude and inclination up to 8 Hz, observed systematically lower amplitudes during outburst decay than rise, and showed that a precessing hot flow model with spin-orbit misalignment of about 10-15 degrees can reproduce the observed amplitudes.
AI.conclusion: Type-C QPO amplitudes in black hole LMXBs are strongly dependent on jet inclination, supporting a geometrical origin scenario, and their variation with outburst phase provides a critical benchmark for theoretical models, especially those involving precessing hot flows with spin-orbit misalignment.

title: Testing cosmic anisotropy with the Combo correlation of gamma-ray bursts
summary: We employ the sample of 244 gamma-ray bursts (GRBs; i.e., C244) with the Combo correlation to test cosmic anisotropy. Meanwhile, the Pantheon sample is introduced to verify whether the GRB sample can suppress the fake anisotropic signals induced by inhomogeneous spatial distributions. In the dipole fitting (DF) method, under the dipole-modulated $Λ$CDM model, the C244 sample shifts the best-fitting longitude $l$ derived from the Pantheon sample by $54.09^\circ$ and reduces the uncertainty in $l$ by approximately $40\%$. Compared to the 118 GRBs (i.e., A118) with the $E_\mathrm{p}$-$E_\mathrm{iso}$ correlation, the shift in longitude $l$ increases by additional $21.35^\circ$. In the hemisphere comparison (HC) method, the preferred direction derived from the C244+Pantheon sample deviates from that of the Pantheon-only sample by more than $1σ$. In contrast, the preferred direction from the A118+Pantheon sample is consistent with the Pantheon-only result within the $1σ$ uncertainty. The preferred direction changes significantly as the number of GRBs increases from 118 to 244. Our results show that a larger GRB sample can reduce the fake anisotropic signals caused by inhomogeneous spatial distributions. Accordingly, we suggest that GRBs have the potential to provide a reliable probe of cosmic anisotropy.

AI.tldr: Using an expanded sample of 244 GRBs and the Pantheon dataset, the study shows increased GRB data reduces false signals of cosmic anisotropy and supports GRBs as effective tools for probing universal anisotropy.
AI.motivation: To test cosmic anisotropy using gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) as probes, while addressing the influence of inhomogeneous spatial distributions that could induce fake anisotropic signals.
AI.method: Utilized a sample of 244 GRBs with the Combo correlation under a dipole-modulated ΛCDM model, verified against the Pantheon supernova sample; applied dipole fitting (DF) and hemisphere comparison (HC) methods to analyze anisotropy.
AI.result: The larger GRB sample (C244) significantly shifted and reduced uncertainty in the preferred longitude direction compared to the smaller 118 GRB sample (A118) and Pantheon alone; combined C244+Pantheon sample also showed directional deviations beyond 1σ, unlike A118+Pantheon; this indicates increased sample size decreases fake anisotropic signals from spatial inhomogeneity.
AI.conclusion: Gamma-ray bursts, especially in larger samples, hold promise as reliable probes for detecting cosmic anisotropy by mitigating artifacts from uneven spatial distributions.

title: Entropic backreaction from cosmic structure formation: a thermodynamic approach to the late-time cosmological tensions
summary: High-precision cosmological observations have revealed persistent tensions within the standard $Λ$CDM paradigm, most notably the discrepancy in the Hubble constant and the lower than predicted amplitude of late-time matter clustering quantified by $S_8$. We propose a unified thermodynamic framework in which entropic backreaction generated during cosmic structure formation modifies both the background expansion history and the growth of matter perturbations. As gravitational instability drives the growth of cosmic structures, the configuration entropy associated with the matter distribution decreases through the nonlinear redistribution of gravitational binding energy. The resulting entropic energy density contributes a late-time backreaction that enhances the cosmic expansion rate without altering early-Universe physics or the CMB sound horizon. Simultaneously, the same irreversible entropy dissipation process induces a dissipative correction within the cosmic velocity flow, suppressing the efficiency of coherent gravitational clustering at late times. The framework operates entirely within standard General Relativity: the Einstein field equations, Poisson equation, and gravitational coupling remain unmodified, and no new propagating degrees of freedom or fifth forces are introduced. Entropic backreaction therefore provides a thermodynamically motivated, theoretically conservative, and observationally testable mechanism that may simultaneously alleviate the major late-time cosmological tensions.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a thermodynamic mechanism where entropy changes during cosmic structure formation modify expansion and matter clustering, addressing key late-time cosmological tensions without new physics beyond General Relativity.
AI.motivation: Persistent tensions in the standard ΛCDM model, specifically in the Hubble constant and S_8 parameter, motivate a revised framework to reconcile observations.
AI.method: A unified thermodynamic framework is proposed where entropic backreaction from cosmic structure formation modifies expansion and matter perturbation growth, without altering fundamental gravitational equations or introducing new forces.
AI.result: Entropic energy density enhances late-time cosmic expansion and entropy dissipation suppresses coherent gravitational clustering, potentially resolving discrepancies in late-time cosmological observations while preserving early-Universe physics.
AI.conclusion: Entropic backreaction arising from structure formation offers a theoretically consistent and observationally testable mechanism within standard General Relativity to alleviate major late-time cosmological tensions, such as those related to the Hubble constant and S_8 amplitude.

title: Can COSI detect $γ$-ray lines from rare isotopes produced in the astrophysical intermediate neutron-capture process?
comment: Submitted to Phys. Rev. Lett., revision requested. Comments welcome
summary: We investigate the nuclear $γ$-ray line emission from rare isotopes produced in the astrophysical intermediate neutron-capture process ($i$ process) and assess the prospects of observing these emissions with $γ$-ray telescopes. The astrophysical sites of the $i$ process remain uncertain, but two candidates with predicted rapid mass ejections at metallicities of stars in the solar neighborhood are post-asymptotic giant branch (post-AGB) stars, such as Sakurai's object (V4334 Sagittarii), and rapidly-accreting white dwarfs (RAWDs). Detailed 1D and 3D simulations indicate that the convective-reactive fluid dynamics responsible for $i$-process nucleosynthesis can lead to violent, non-radial outbursts resulting in mass ejections of $i$-process products. We calculate ejected yields of rare isotopes whose radioactive decays may produce detectable $γ$-ray lines, particularly in the 0.5-2 MeV range, focusing on $^{22}$Na, $^{89}$Sr, and $^{95}$Zr. We estimate the formation rates of these sources and the likelihood of detecting their $γ$-ray emissions within 1000 parsecs of the Sun. The probability of observing $i$-process emission lines during COSI's operational period is up to $\approx 1\%$, rising to $11\%$ for $^{89}$Sr if observed within a few days. Due to the long lifetime and large production of $^{22}$Na from proton-capture reactions its detection is more likely, with a probability of $\approx 5\%$. Future space missions could increase the observation probability to several tens of percent. Detection of long-lived neutron-rich isotopes such as $^{137}$Cs would provide the first direct $γ$-ray signature of intermediate neutron-density nucleosynthesis, distinguishing the $i$ process from classical s- and r-process pathways. (abridged)

AI.tldr: This paper investigates gamma-ray emissions from rare isotopes produced by the intermediate neutron-capture process in astrophysical objects, calculates their yields through simulations, estimates detection probabilities with gamma-ray telescopes, and finds that while detection is challenging, it is possible and would provide unique confirmation of the i process distinct from other nucleosynthesis.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to explore the nuclear gamma-ray line emission signatures from rare isotopes generated by the i process, an astrophysical nucleosynthesis pathway whose sites remain uncertain. Detecting these emissions would provide direct evidence of i-process nucleosynthesis and distinguish it from classical s- and r-processes.
AI.method: The approach involves detailed 1D and 3D simulations of convective-reactive fluid dynamics in candidate astrophysical sites (post-AGB stars and rapidly-accreting white dwarfs) to calculate yields of rare isotopes. These yields inform estimates of gamma-ray line emissions and formation rates, used to assess detection probabilities within 1000 parsecs using current and future gamma-ray observatories.
AI.result: The results indicate detection probabilities for i-process gamma-ray lines during the COSI mission period up to ~1%, with higher probabilities (~11%) for short-lived isotopes like 89Sr if observed promptly. The longer-lived isotope 22Na has a ~5% detection probability due to its higher production yield. Future missions could raise these probabilities to several tens of percent.
AI.conclusion: The study concludes that gamma-ray emissions from rare isotopes produced in the astrophysical intermediate neutron-capture process (i process) have a low but non-negligible probability of detection with current and future gamma-ray telescopes, offering a unique diagnostic to distinguish the i process from other nucleosynthesis pathways.

title: Whispers of Supergravity in Gravitational Wave Backgrounds: Determining the Gravitino Mass from Cosmic Thermal History
summary: Gravitino masses above the electroweak scale provide the simplest solution to the gravitino problem, but such large mass scales lie far beyond the reach of collider experiments. We show that the stochastic gravitational wave background offers a direct probe of this otherwise inaccessible regime. Despite decaying before Big-Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN), these gravitinos naturally generate a period of early matter domination in the early universe. This non-standard epoch leaves a characteristic imprint on any primordial gravitational wave background, characterised by two frequencies corresponding to the onset and end of this phase. We demonstrate that these features can be used to directly infer both the gravitino mass and its initial abundance in a direct mapping. Future gravitational wave observatories span a vast frequency range, enabling sensitivity to gravitino masses from the BBN bound of $\mathcal{O}(100)\,\text{TeV}$ all the way up to $\mathcal{O}(10^{10})\,\text{TeV}$, with recent signal by NANOGrav already probing masses in the range $500$-$10^4$ TeV. Gravitational wave observables therefore probe an enormous region of parameter space, far beyond the reach of collider experiments. We are entering an era in which supergravity can be probed through gravitational wave backgrounds alongside collider experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using the stochastic gravitational wave background to detect heavy gravitinos by their early matter domination imprint, enabling measurement of gravitino properties across a large mass range inaccessible to colliders.
AI.motivation: Large gravitino masses provide a solution to the gravitino problem but are inaccessible to collider experiments, motivating alternative probes.
AI.method: The paper investigates the imprint of an early matter domination phase caused by heavy gravitinos on the primordial stochastic gravitational wave background, identifying characteristic frequency features.
AI.result: They show that gravitational wave observatories can detect these features, enabling direct determination of gravitino mass and abundance across a wide mass range, including ranges probed by NANOGrav signals.
AI.conclusion: Stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds provide a direct and powerful probe of high-scale gravitino physics, opening new avenues to test supergravity beyond collider capabilities.

title: Fermi-LAT View on Three Ultra-high-energy 1LHAASO Sources in the $52^{\circ}<l<55^{\circ}$ Region
summary: Using more than 17 yr of Fermi-LAT data, we performed a detailed investigation of the complex $52^{\circ}<l<55^{\circ}$ region, which encompasses the three ultra-high-energy sources 1LHAASO J1928+1746u, 1LHAASO J1928+1813u, and 1LHAASO J1929+1846u.This region hosts multiple SNRs, pulsars, GeV and TeV sources. Our analysis resolves the GeV emission into three pointlike sources (J1925+1729P, J1930+1851P, and J1932+1916P) and two extended sources (J1929+1732E and J1930+1826E), and improves significantly on the description based on the 4FGL-DR4 catalog. Source J1932+1916P is identified as the known gamma-ray pulsar PSR J1932+1916, while J1925+1729P may be a new gamma-ray pulsar candidate distinct from the known gamma-ray pulsar PSR J1925+1720. This warrants future investigation and a search for pulsations. Source J1930+1851P coincides with the TeV source PWN/SNR G54.1+0.3 and its GeV-TeV spectrum is consistent with both leptonic and hadronic interpretations, although a leptonic origin in relation to the known PWN is more likely. The GeV-TeV spectrum of J1929+1732E is consistent with a hybrid lepto-hadronic scenario in which the TeV emission traces the PWN powered by the pulsar PSR J1928+1746, while the GeV emission may result from interactions between particles escaped from the parent SNR and illuminating the gas environment. Similarly, J1930+1826E is likely connected to PWN/SNR G54.1+0.3 under a hadronic scenario involving escaped particles in their early propagation stage. Owing to spectral and/or morphological mismatches, the connection of these five GeV sources to the three LHAASO sources is not clear. This warrants deeper observations with HAWC and LHAASO, and a dedicated study of the modeling of the Galactic diffuse emission. Future CTAO observations with higher angular resolution are expected to deliver crucial information for the study of this region.

AI.tldr: A 17-year Fermi-LAT study resolves complex gamma-ray emissions in the $52^{\circ}<l<55^{\circ}$ Galactic region into five sources with varying origins, suggesting leptonic, hadronic, and hybrid scenarios. No clear link to three ultra-high-energy LHAASO sources was found, prompting the need for deeper, higher-resolution observations to better understand these high-energy phenomena.
AI.motivation: To investigate the complex $52^{\circ}<l<55^{\circ}$ region containing ultra-high-energy sources and multiple astrophysical objects (SNRs, pulsars, GeV and TeV sources) using extensive Fermi-LAT data, and to improve the understanding of GeV emission sources in this region.
AI.method: Using more than 17 years of Fermi-LAT gamma-ray data, the study performed a detailed spectral and morphological analysis to resolve the GeV emission into discrete sources, identifying pointlike and extended sources and comparing their spectral features with existing catalogs and TeV observations.
AI.result: The analysis resolved the GeV emission into three pointlike sources and two extended sources, with identifications including known and candidate gamma-ray pulsars and sources associated with PWNe/SNRs. Spectral studies suggested leptonic, hadronic, and hybrid lepto-hadronic emission scenarios, but no clear association between the GeV sources and the three LHAASO ultra-high-energy sources was established. The study highlighted the need for deeper multi-instrument observations and advanced modeling of Galactic diffuse emission.
AI.conclusion: The Fermi-LAT data analysis significantly improved source characterization in the $52^{\circ}<l<55^{\circ}$ region, revealing complex emission components with multiple possible origins. However, uncertainties remain regarding the connection between GeV sources and ultra-high-energy LHAASO sources, necessitating further high-resolution gamma-ray observations and refined diffuse emission models to clarify the nature of these sources.

title: Fewer simulations, sharper covariances: Reducing mock covariance noise with Zeldovich approximation control variates
summary: We present a control-variate method for reducing the variance of power spectrum covariance matrix estimates from simulations of large-scale structure. The key idea is to pair each mock simulation with a cheap Zeldovich-approximation realization sharing the same initial conditions, and to use the known statistical properties of the Zeldovich field to remove correlated sample variance from the covariance estimator. Under a Gaussian disconnected approximation, we derive fully analytic expressions for both the optimal control-variate coefficient, $β(k,\ell;k',\ell')$, and the corresponding correlation, $ρ(k,\ell;k',\ell')$, in terms of the auto- and cross-power spectra of the target and control fields. In the monopole case, the correlation takes the particularly simple form $ρ(k,k') = r^2(k),r^2(k')$, where $r(k)$ is the standard cross-correlation coefficient between the target and Zeldovich fields, implying that covariance estimation remains highly efficient whenever the two fields are strongly correlated. For masked redshift-space lognormal mocks, resembling Luminous Red Galaxies from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), we find that the control-variate estimator reduces the variance of the covariance matrix by approximately an order of magnitude on large scales, $k \lesssim 0.05\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$, precisely where accurate covariance estimation is most challenging. The gains are smaller for higher $k$ but typically accelerate convergence by a factor of 2-3, substantially lowering the computational cost of covariance estimation for current and upcoming large-scale structure surveys. Due to its simplicity, this method is readily implementable in current imaging and spectroscopic surveys (e.g., DESI, Euclid, LSST, PFS, SPHEREx).

AI.tldr: A control-variate approach using Zeldovich-approximation realizations significantly reduces variance in power spectrum covariance estimates from simulations, improving efficiency and lowering computational cost for large-scale structure cosmology.
AI.motivation: Accurate covariance matrix estimation from simulations of large-scale structure is computationally expensive, particularly on large scales where sample variance is significant.
AI.method: Introduce a control-variate technique that pairs each mock simulation with a cheap Zeldovich-approximation realization sharing the same initial conditions, using the Zeldovich field's known statistical properties to analytically reduce variance in the covariance estimates under a Gaussian disconnected approximation.
AI.result: The control-variate estimator reduces covariance matrix variance by about an order of magnitude on large scales (k ≲ 0.05 h/Mpc), and improves convergence by factors of 2-3 on smaller scales, significantly lowering computational costs for covariance estimation in various cosmological surveys.
AI.conclusion: The proposed control-variate method effectively leverages the correlation between target and Zeldovich fields to substantially reduce variance in covariance matrix estimates, is analytically tractable, and is straightforward to implement in current and future large-scale structure surveys.

title: Mass and radius measurements of the neutron star 47~Tuc X7 -- A new bias-free method
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A. Data files available in Zenodo
summary: Neutron star (NS) radius measurements provide precious information to constrain the dense matter equation of state (EOS). Quiescent low-mass X-ray binaries (qLMXBs) have been used for this purpose, but a number of sources of systematic biases were uncovered, making other sources more favored for EOS studies. We aim to reintroduce qLMXBs as reliable sources of NS mass and radius measurements with a new method, free of systematic biases. We test our implementation on the qLMXB X7 in the globular cluster 47 Tucanae. We used X-PSI to perform the spectral analysis of the 47Tuc X7 observations. X-PSI accurately models the effects of the unknown NS rotation and possible surface anisotropies (two sources of biases in qLMXBs) on the NS spectra. The most significant source of bias on the radius is usually the chemical composition of the NS atmosphere, which, in the case of 47Tuc X7, is known to be hydrogen-rich. A broad range of masses and radii was explored. We obtain a NS radius at 1.4 $M_\odot$ of $R_{1.4} = 12.9\pm0.4$ km (68% credible interval). A shift of the radius by less than a % is measured compared to the model where these sources of systematic uncertainties are neglected. More importantly, including rotation and surface anisotropies in the modeling does not significantly broaden the radius posteriors. We also place strong constraints on the X-ray pulsed fraction (upper limit of 6.0% at a 99.97% credible level) caused by the possible presence of a hot spot. This suggests that, for 47Tuc X7, robust radius constraints can be obtained even without considering systematics, likely because of the deep exposures. We use the resulting M-R constraints from this NS to quantify the improvement on an EOS inference when combined with other measurements. We show that, using recently developed tools, qLMXBs can be exploited to infer reliable NS masses and radii, which can in turn constrain the EOS.

AI.tldr: By accurately modeling rotation and surface effects in qLMXB 47Tuc X7, this study obtains precise neutron star radius measurements with minimal bias, reestablishing qLMXBs as valuable sources for constraining the dense matter equation of state.
AI.motivation: To reintroduce quiescent low-mass X-ray binaries (qLMXBs) as reliable sources for neutron star (NS) mass and radius measurements, overcoming previously identified systematic biases.
AI.method: Spectral analysis of qLMXB X7 in 47 Tucanae using X-PSI, which models NS rotation and surface anisotropies to mitigate biases; exploration of a broad range of NS masses and radii with known hydrogen-rich atmospheric composition.
AI.result: Determined NS radius at 1.4 solar masses as 12.9±0.4 km with minimal bias (<1%) from systematic effects; rotation and surface anisotropies inclusion does not significantly widen radius constraints; tight upper limit on X-ray pulsed fraction (6.0%) indicating robust radius measurement.
AI.conclusion: qLMXBs, when modeled with advanced tools accounting for rotation and surface anisotropies, provide reliable mass and radius measurements for NSs, enabling robust constraints on the dense matter equation of state, especially when combined with other observations.

title: Magnetic Configuration Imprints on Quasi-Periodic Variability in GRMHD Simulations of Thin Accretion Disks
summary: The origin of quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in black hole accretion flow remains uncertain, particularly regarding the role of magnetic field configurations in shaping disk structure and variability signatures. We investigate this using global two- and three-dimensional (2D and 3D) general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations of geometrically thin disks initialized with different multi-loop magnetic field configurations. These configurations naturally produce a puffed-up inner region. We find that QPO-like variability arises in the effective viscosity and mass accretion rate, with frequencies following the local radial epicyclic frequency and its harmonics. Time-series diagrams show coherent, inclined stripe-like patterns associated with inertial-acoustic perturbations, while power spectra exhibit narrow bands of enhanced variability linked to truncation radii associated with magnetic fields. Cross-correlation analysis reveals a finite lag between pressure and Maxwell stress at these interfaces, consistent with viscous-epicyclic overstability. The magnetic topology regulates both the truncation radius and the location of resonant cavities that sustain oscillations. As the disk becomes thicker, increased turbulent diffusion suppresses the overstability and the associated QPO signals. We find that the QPO frequency ranges and their evolution are consistent with observations of black hole X-ray binaries during outbursts. These results suggest that magnetic field configurations play a pivotal role in shaping disk structure and variability in accreting black holes.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates through GRMHD simulations that magnetic field configurations in thin black hole accretion disks induce quasi-periodic oscillations consistent with observations, by shaping disk structure, resonant cavities, and viscous-epicyclic overstability effects.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to understand the origin of quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in black hole accretion flows, focusing on how different magnetic field configurations affect disk structure and variability.
AI.method: The study employs global 2D and 3D general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations of geometrically thin accretion disks with various multi-loop magnetic field setups to analyze resulting disk behaviors and variability.
AI.result: QPO-like variability is observed in effective viscosity and accretion rate, linked to local radial epicyclic frequencies and harmonics. Magnetic topology controls disk truncation radii and resonant cavities, influencing oscillation patterns. Increased disk thickness and turbulence suppress overstability and QPO signals. Frequency ranges match observations from black hole X-ray binaries.
AI.conclusion: Magnetic field configurations critically influence the structure and variability of accretion disks around black holes, providing a plausible mechanism for observed QPOs through viscous-epicyclic overstability associated with magnetic truncation.
